judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse has two conflicting return contracts: it returns the full safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), but the Google call site (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~95) treats it as the parsed value and persists the Zod envelope as the credential key via prisma.credential.update — every token refresh overwrites the stored Google credential with { success: true, data: ... }, so the next instantiation/refresh fails; silent OAuth-token data loss for all deployments, not just credential-sync users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data`. However, in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the call site assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This would store the Zod envelope (e.g., `{ success: true, data: ... }`) as the credential `key`, corrupting the stored credential shape and likely breaking subsequent uses that expect the raw credential fields (access_token, refresh_token, expiry_date, etc.). Other call sites (e.g., Office365/Salesforce) treat the return value as a safeParse result, confirming the contract mismatch at the Google call site.
